comment: CANONICAL debugger-side trace bring-up catalog (bkpt-packages/trace-support). Consumers bundle a snapshot at build/dev time (the ViewAlyzer app never fetches at runtime; a future app fetch would come from this repo). Offline user override: <userAppData>/ViewAlyzer/trace-support.json (same shape). Rows are keyed by debug ARCHITECTURE, not by chip: one row covers every part sharing a vendor debug-domain map, so this file stays a handful of rows forever. A row matches when probing its idcode_addr over the debug connection reads a nonzero device id (optionally restricted to dev_id). Its init ops then run through a read-modify-write interpreter: {addr, set} = write literal, {addr, or} = OR bits in, {addr, insert, mask} = (old & ~mask) | (insert & mask). The token $prescaler resolves to (cpu-clock-hz / swo-freq-hz) - 1. tpiu:false means the row replaces the standard ARM TPIU programming (parts with their own SWO block). Optional per-row keys: onchip = the vacore_capture --probeless profile token for the family (Auto chip selection in the on-chip trace flow; absent = generic discovery), note = a one-line caveat logged when the row matches (for example: SWO bring-up not catalogued for this family yet). Rows are probed IN ORDER and the first match wins, so rows with a dev_id list must precede match-any rows whose idcode address aliases on other parts.

devices.name: stm32h7

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: D1/D3 debug clocks + trace clock enable
SWO SPPR: async NRZ (replaces the standard TPIU block)
RCC AHB4ENR: GPIOB clock (SWO pin = PB3)
GPIOB OSPEEDR: PB3 very high speed

devices.comment: Auto resolves 0x450 to the single-core h7 profile; a dual-core H745/H755 (same dev_id) needs the h755-cm7 override.

devices.name: stm32h7rs
devices.note: STM32H7R/S: on-chip trace is supported; SWO bring-up rows are not catalogued for this family yet, so SWO needs firmware-side bring-up.

devices.name: stm32n6
devices.note: STM32N6: on-chip trace (ETR) is supported; SWO bring-up rows are not catalogued for this family yet, so SWO needs firmware-side bring-up.
devices.comment: Must precede the match-any M33 row: 0xE0044000 reads a nonzero word on this part.

match.comment: DBGMCU as seen from the Cortex-M33 core AP (AP1 on H5); AP0 aliases it at 0xE0044000 but the products program through the core AP. dev_id 0x474 = H503 (verified on the rack 2026-08-28: IDCODE 0x10036474), 0x484 = H56x/H573. Listed before the match-any rows.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_EN + TRACE_IOEN + DBG_STOP/STANDBY, TRACE_MODE=00 async SWO (same bit layout as the U5/L5 generation; RM0492 DBGMCU_CR). Without TRACE_EN the TPIU is absent from the bus.

match.comment: DBGMCU for the TrustZone Cortex-M33 generation (U5/L5/WBA all map DBGMCU here; H5 does not). dev_id 0x482 (U575/585) verified on silicon 2026-07-11; other family ids match by architecture.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_EN (trace clock gate — without it the TPIU is absent from the bus: accesses bus-fault AND wedge the ST-LINK DAP until probe power-cycle) + TRACE_IOEN + DBG_STOP/STANDBY; TRACE_MODE=00 async SWO
DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_IOEN + DBG_SLEEP/STOP/STANDBY (keeps trace clocked through WFI idles)
